content: The forehead, also referred to as the brow in human anatomy, is the bony region of the skull located above the eyes. In modern humans, the forehead is approximately vertical in orientation and extends upward to the hairline, where the contour of the head becomes flatter. The muscles associated with the forehead include the frontalis muscle, which is responsible for moving and contracting the scalp in this region. Historically, the pronunciation of the word forehead rhymed with horrid. In Received Pronunciation (RP) and General American (GenAm) English, this was represented phonetically as /ˈfɒrɪd/ or /ˈfɔːrɪd/. However, in more recent years, the spelling-based pronunciation /ˈfɔːrhɛd/ in RP and /ˈfɔːrhɛd/ in GenAm has become increasingly prevalent.
